mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent discount rate expectations and reduced liquidity in risk assets.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the 20-day return when FEDFUNDS ≤ 5.0 (p > 0.05, two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a labor market softening that precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by > 1% month-over-month
regime_hint: Early warning of recession in US labor market
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 such triggered events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (cumulative probability ≤ 0.67).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects strengthening consumer confidence and demand for equity-backed housing-related businesses.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 60-day window following the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to the 60-day return during the prior three months' average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 10% in a single month is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to expectations of future supply-side shocks and reduced corporate earnings momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 10% in a single month
failure_condition: In 40% of such events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (cumulative probability ≤ 0.60).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly increases by more than 0.3% in a month while the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged, the S&P 500 5-day forward return tends to be positive as inflation expectations are reassessed upward.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3% month-over-month with FEDFUNDS unchanged
regime_hint: Unexpected inflation surprise in a hold-rate environment
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 5-day return during prior months with lower CPIAUCSL surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% and a rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 20,000 for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market tightening supports equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS increases by > 20,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 out of 25 such triggered windows, the 20-day forward return is not positive (cumulative probability ≤ 0.60).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: a prolonged drop in RSAFS below 700M for three months) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to weakening consumer demand and reduced corporate earnings growth.
regime_hint: Prolonged weakness in business demand proxies
failure_condition: During the 60-day window following the trigger, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 60-day average during the prior three months' average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and home sales (HOUST) both fall by at least 8% in the same month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to dual supply-side pressures and reduced corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥ 8% and HOUST decreases by ≥ 8% in the same month
failure_condition: In 50% of such triggered months, the 20-day forward return is not negative (cumulative probability ≤ 0.50).
